statement.p: Find \int_C\vec F\cdot d\vec r for \vec F = -4 y\,\vec i -2 x\,\vec j + 2 z\,\vec k if C is the helix x=\cos t, y=\sin t, z=t, for 0\le t\le 4\pi.

static.solution: C is given by \vec r=\cos t\,\vec i+\sin t\,\vec j +t\,\vec k, we have \vec r'(t)=-\sin t\,\vec i+\cos t\,\vec j +\vec k. Thus, \int_C\vec F\cdot d\vec r = \int_0^{4\pi}(4\sin t\, \vec i - 2 \cos t\,\vec j + 2 t\,\vec k)\cdot(-\sin t\,\vec i+\cos t\,\vec j +\vec k) dt = \int_0^{4\pi}(-4 \sin^2 t - 2 \cos^2 t + 2 t) dt = 4\pi + 16\pi^2.
